subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-profile pool-routing config/API now, or keep this work split into narrower auth-profile rotation, quota/bucket cooldown, and provider/probe fixes first?
rationale: Source inspection shows a real missing capability, but the requested solution defines public config, persisted state, fallback semantics, and session stickiness behavior that automation should not invent without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design additive core pool routing
options.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with explicit defaults, one initial strategy, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

options.title: Phase narrower fixes first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker while solving quota buckets, same-provider retry depth, and model/auth binding in separate focused issues first.

options.title: Defer to plugin or sidecar exploration
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged until an external prototype proves the missing plugin/API seam and native surface is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Sponsor a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool contract with explicit defaults, one initial strategy, status/probe observability, and upgrade-safe config handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice spans auth config, provider routing, fallback behavior, and session semantics, where steipete has the strongest history signal among the identified owners.
